headline: EPS growth continues; bookings soften, revenue view trimmed
summary_short: Accenture's Q3 FY2026 (labeled FY2026 Q2 on this shard) revenue rose 6% y/y to $18.72 billion, with diluted EPS up 9% to $3.80 and operating margin expanding 20bps to 17.0%, even as new bookings fell 2% y/y to $19.3 billion.
summary_long: Revenue grew 6% y/y (3% local currency) to $18.72B, slightly above the midpoint of guidance, led by Managed Services (+8% USD) and EMEA (+10% USD). Operating margin expanded 20bps to 17.0% as lower SG&A intensity offset a 10bp gross-margin decline. Diluted EPS rose 9% to $3.80 on higher operating results and a lower share count, partly offset by a higher tax rate. New bookings fell 2% y/y to $19.32B. Free cash flow was $3.60B; cash fell to $10.2B from $11.5B at fiscal year-start after $2.2B returned to shareholders. Accenture narrowed full-year revenue-growth guidance to 3%-4% local currency, while raising EPS and capital-return guidance.
